records.name: Adygea
records.current_summary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta), checked against the dossier and fetched sources: a North Caucasus republic, within the region that foreign travel advisories name as dangerous for LGBT+ people, where monitors report 'no safe life' for LGBT+ residents; the federal 'extremism' machinery applies nationwide (101 convictions by June 2025). Scored relative to the national score (0.12) for Russia.

sources.claim: UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity and expression (June 2025): LGB people generally not assessed as at state-persecution risk, but North Caucasus residents, trans people and public LGBT+ activists likely face persecution; same-sex marriage and gender transition banned, trans healthcare effectively banned 2023, no discrimination protections; at least 139 people affected by anti-LGBT laws 2022-2024.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (Cloudflare block); the underlying US State Department travel advisory for Russia covers general travel safety and, per the research dossier, the North Caucasus republics and interior-permission entry regimes.

Human Rights Watch news report (30 June 2025): 101 'extremism' convictions for alleged participation in the banned international LGBT movement or display of its symbols - 98 administrative, 3 criminal; 20 criminal cases January 2024-June 2025 (2 prison sentences, 1 death in pretrial detention, 17 pending); 81 people convicted of administrative symbol offenses since January 2024, most of them on Russia's largest social media platform (61); publishing-house staff charged May 2025 facing up to 12 years.

sources.claim: UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity (June 2025): no specific law criminalising LGBT+ identity as such, but at least 139 individuals affected by anti-LGBT+ laws including 'gay propaganda' convictions, detentions and 'extremism' prosecutions; no SOGI discrimination legislation; the note's central distinction is that general state risk is not established across the country except in the North Caucasus, and it notes there is no reliable data on the size or distribution of the LGBT+ population.

Human Rights Watch (30 June 2025): courts issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions for participation in or display of symbols of the alleged 'International LGBT Movement'; repeated display of a banned symbol carries up to four years' imprisonment; cases include forced labour after posting a rainbow flag on social media, and administrative sentences that prompted users to delete accounts out of fear of prosecution.

flags: Scored relative to the national score (0.12) for Russia
